title: 1977 AHSME Problem 25
statement: Determine the largest positive integer \(n\) such that \(1005!\) is divisible by \(10^n.\)

solutions.text:
There are more factors of \(2\) than of \(5,\) so the exponent of \(10\) is \[ \begin{aligned} n={}&\left\lfloor\frac{1005}{5}\right\rfloor+ \left\lfloor\frac{1005}{25}\right\rfloor\\ &+\left\lfloor\frac{1005}{125}\right\rfloor+ \left\lfloor\frac{1005}{625}\right\rfloor\\ ={}&201+40+8+1=250. \end{aligned} \] Since \(250\) is not listed, the correct choice is “none of these.”

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Include contributions from multiples of \(25,\) \(125,\) and \(625\)
